P1.evidence: No setter code in the title and no setter is referenced anywhere in the call, so the read-back check does not apply. The frame was three parts of four: 'It's an opportunity, right, for me to understand you. You know, where are you today? Where do you want to be? If we can help, I can show you some options' — 'what's in the way' and 'what you need' were both omitted. Agreement was implicit only, a trailing 'okay?' answered with 'Oh, okay', rather than an explicit 'does that work?'. The opening question was clean: 'what really is the biggest reason that has had you wanting to explore getting kettlebell coaching?'

P2.evidence: The weakest phase and the one with the most consequence. Age was never asked — the prospect volunteered '43 now' in passing and the rep reflected it back later — and height and weight were never obtained at all, on a call that closed a body-composition programme for a self-described hardgainer. Work was covered conversationally rather than as a check, and the desk-bound question was answered only because the prospect volunteered 'we are basically sitting all day long, I can't leave the cockpit seat'. Health conditions and injuries were never asked in any form: the new knee strain surfaced only because the prospect raised pickleball himself, and the rep did not follow up on it once. Diet was never asked despite nutrition being pillar two. Sleep was never asked despite the prospect describing 2 a.m. wake-ups and four-to-five-hour nights, which the rep acknowledged with 'Wow' and moved past. Energy was never asked. Training week was partially reconstructed from the guilt-cycle description rather than elicited.

P3.evidence: The best-run discovery in the call. The genie question landed the surface goal — 'you want to look and feel stronger and fitter... And bigger' — and the bridge past the physical was textbook: 'beyond the surface level, I guess the deeper question for yourself, Shaz, is who do you really want to become?' That produced the single most valuable line on the call: 'it's nothing to do with my physical appearance. I just want to be mentally confident. I want to be able to do things that I set down to do.' The rep then pushed one level further with 'Why is that important for you, to be congruent?' and got the career-change identity story. The reflect-back was delivered well as 'to step into Shaz 2.0, the higher version of yourself, who's mentally sharp and congruent'. What was missed: no question about a physical thing he wants to do but can't, and the ripple-effect moves were asserted rather than asked — 'Your marriage, your relationships, how you carry yourself as a pilot in your work. These are the ripple effects that we're more interested in' is the rep telling him who else it impacts instead of making him say it.

P4.evidence: Cleanly run. 'why haven't you brought in a coach in Vietnam, in Da Nang?' produced the real structural blocker — every coach he has met demanded a fixed weekly time commitment his roster cannot support. 'knowing that you're driven by having structure, routine, goals to aim for, why haven't you been able to find that over the past 10 years?' pushed root cause, and 'What is the voice at the back of your mind that speaks when you know you should be working out?' got him to name it himself: 'I guess one of the main reasons is I don't have a program. And more importantly, I haven't set a goal because a goal gives you a timeline.' The self-sufficiency challenge ran in the scripted spirit: 'if I wanted to get a six pack, and all I did was watch videos on YouTube, I would never get it... there's a big difference between people who say and people who do.'

P5.evidence: The consequence question was asked but without the time horizon that gives it weight: 'what's the consequence if you don't take that step? What does that mean?' It still worked — 'I'm going to be unhappy with myself, like I've been. And it's like a spiral, because I know I'm falling, but I don't want to hit rock bottom' — but the rep did not follow with 'are you willing to settle for that' or 'why not', so the answer was never sharpened. The line in the sand was the strongest single moment of the call: 'are you actually ready to take that step?' answered with 'I guess I am, yes' and immediately challenged with 'You guess, or are you ready?' Substituting 'Would you say this is a want or a need?' for the settle-for question is a recurring habit of this rep and it collects a softer answer.

P6.evidence: Correct sequencing, which is the important thing — both commitment checks were run before any price was mentioned, unlike the same rep's earlier call in this batch. The trust gauge produced a genuine 10 out of 10 with a substantive reason, and the capability check was explicit: 'do you feel internally capable of actually seeing this through?' — 'Yes, I do.' The rep only moved to price after that. Missing entirely is the all-in question — 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in on this?' — which is the one that surfaces hidden blockers, and its absence is why the prospect's roster problem was never fully isolated before the close.

P11.evidence: The phase was reached and then made unobservable. Payment collection was initiated on the call — 'We process the investment, get through the next steps, I onboard you' — and the rep immediately announced 'I'll remove my Fathom note-taker, okay? I'm going to take sensitive information', which is where the recording ends. The Trevor call was described as an intent rather than booked live: 'then I'll book the call with Trevor next week'. Whether the agreement email was confirmed and signed on the call, and whether the welcome email, Skool link and onboarding questionnaire were walked through, cannot be assessed at all from this recording, so those two checks are marked not applicable rather than scored as failures the rep may not have committed.

objection_plays.detail: The timing objection was raised in substance and early — 'it's my working hours that are so irregular. They kind of discourage me from committing to a program' — supported by the detail that every coach he has approached wanted a fixed weekly slot. The rep answered it, but with the offer's features rather than the play: 'we want the next program you enter to be the final one for you... it being adjusting to your life, not the other way around', then the 30-minute session length and the 5-10 minute mobility block. None of the scripted moves ran — no 'things never slow down, when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled', which was the single most on-point line available and was never used. It resolved anyway because the efficiency reframe genuinely addressed his stated blocker.

SCRIPT GAP — structural scheduling impossibility. Objection D assumes a busy season that will pass. This prospect's constraint is permanent and occupational: a rostered airline captain waking at 2 a.m., flying 12-hour days and sleeping four to five hours. 'Things never slow down' is not a rebuttal here, it is a concession. There is no scripted path for a shift worker whose availability genuinely cannot be predicted week to week, and this is the exact profile the programme's flexibility claim is most attractive to and least tested against.

SCRIPT GAP — recovery capacity. The prospect disclosed chronic four-to-six-hour sleep, describing six hours as 'luxury', and separately that he does not eat after training because he is only thirsty and can drop 1-2 kg of water weight in a session. Adding three to four loaded kettlebell sessions a week to that is a programming question with no scripted handling. The rep did not raise it, did not qualify against it, and the playbook offers nothing here.

notes: Discovery depth and the pre-price commitment sequence were both good — the identity work in Phase 3 and the 'you guess, or are you ready?' challenge in Phase 5 are worth replaying to the team. The failure is Baseline: nine checks, one partial pair and seven misses, and the rep sold a loaded training programme to a 43-year-old without ever asking his height, weight, diet, sleep, energy, health conditions or injuries. Every one of those facts that did surface came from the prospect volunteering it. Coach the Baseline block as non-negotiable before the pillars, and coach the rep to stop substituting 'want or a need?' for the scripted settle-for question.
